Systems including CRM, Stripe, Bechler, shipping, activation, returns, replacements, and chargebacks are integrated and running smoothly, but demand has declined from 326 calls in April to 198 in July plus 129 retargeting calls, with only about 20 high-intent opportunities. Sales conversion suffered from missed calls and representatives covering three to four companies simultaneously, prompting recommendations for dedicated American sales coverage. Billing discrepancies exist between 60 active units in GoHighLevel and at least 48 to 49 payment-problem accounts requiring cleanup, with leadership needing to assess unpaid accounts, deactivation policies, platform costs, closer costs, and overall operating structure before deciding next steps.
action_items: Sohib to provide Stripe information and verify Medicare or HSA changes.
Abdulla Salem to review payment cleanup for billing discrepancies.
Ameera Salem to review deactivation notice requirements and assess continuation costs versus revenue.
Ameera and Abdulla to decide Life Run's next steps and review customer and unit numbers.
Ameera to discuss status with Roland.

meetings_digest.title: Flow Sync 2.0
key_points: Client review: Account status, work in progress, and next steps were not fully prepared; strategy discussion was postponed.
Leadership gap: Routine messages and task tracking were insufficient; stronger ownership, judgment, and direction are expected.
Compensation: Pay is moving to documented hourly work while the role undergoes formal review.
Employment risk: Continued work may end by January, with approximately two months to demonstrate meaningful, lasting value.
Immediate work: Complete call forwarding, reply to Sheriff Mahadi, confirm Mana Cash’s status, and review client operations.

meetings_digest.title: Meet w/ Sohib & Ameera & Abdulla - LR Updates
key_points: Status: Life Run closure versus relaunch remains undecided; marketing, sales, and related work are paused.
Systems: CRM, Stripe, Bechler, shipping, activation, returns, replacements, and chargebacks workflows are integrated and running smoothly.
Demand: April generated 326 calls, July 198, plus 129 retargeting calls; approximately 20 were high-intent opportunities.
Sales Gap: Missed calls and weak conversion stemmed from representatives covering three or four companies; dedicated American sales coverage was recommended.
Billing: Active units are unclear—60 in GoHighLevel versus at least 48–49 payment-problem accounts; historical billing cleanup remains needed.

meetings_digest.title: MedStation <> Dashboard
key_points: Dashboard: Nearly matches reporting needs; finance, KPI, and data definitions still need alignment.
Reporting: Supports daily reviews, monthly revenue forecasts, KPI tracking, and location-level service views.
Data Rules: Appointments cover January 2025 onward; canceled and rescheduled records are removed.
Marketing ROI: Tracks channel spend, leads, bookings, show rates, revenue, cost-per-lead, and return on ad spend.
Compliance: Aggregate reporting excludes patient names; patient-level views require HIPAA-compliant access.

meetings_digest.title: Flow Sync 2.0
key_points: Delivery Speed: Main build is largely complete; onboarding, access delays, and handoffs remain the biggest launch blockers.
Onboarding: Create one central client record and a 15-minute intake questionnaire before onboarding calls.
Med Station: Ads were ready for two weeks but inactive; Google Business Profile category remains an easy improvement.
Client Work: Manakesh needs web, SEO, Google Ads, budget confirmation, and access; Rob partnership is unlikely to proceed.
Performance: Billy Dough recorded approximately 1,400 ad spend and 6,400 return over the last 30 days.

meetings_digest.title: Medstation GHL Ramp up
key_points: Rollout Goal: Move all five active Medstation clinics onto GHL before year-end; inactive clinics excluded.
Build Plan: Clone Weston’s setup, starting with lower-volume clinics, then higher-volume clinics.
Timeline Risk: Build target is December 18–24; training starts early January, possibly extending to mid-January.
Technical Work: Create clinic-specific WhatsApp numbers, tracking, dashboards, integrations, pipelines, and workflows.
Lead Recovery: Enable 45-day reactivation and build follow-up for 98 interested leads who never booked.

meetings_digest.title: Web/SEO team coordination
key_points: Faster launches: Target client launches within 12–13 days using minor edits, lead magnets, CTAs, forms, GHL, and ads.
Unified onboarding: Combine SEO, web, CRM, and ads details into one form; store call links, access, and client data centrally.
Client records: Maintain one editable master sheet, plus linked strategy briefs covering locations, services, and priorities.
Commercial focus: Shift emphasis toward trade services; retain clients long-term, potentially accepting lower pricing for two-to-four-year relationships.
Location pricing: First three locations stay within base pricing; additional locations may cost $100–$300 each.

meetings_digest.title: Quality HVAC by Fibid | Contract Review
key_points: Google Verification: Escalate missing verification options; submit current signage, Regis invoice, and 12-month lease.
Profile Strategy: Prioritize Fibbit verification; separate Fibbit and Quality HVAC profiles to rebuild visibility.
Marketing Results: Quality HVAC grew strongly; Fibbit stayed flat despite approximately 400 reviews.
SEO Gains: Quality HVAC clicks nearly doubled; average ranking improved from 44 to 14.
Meta ROI: Approximately $2,000 spent over 90 days generated $9,300 revenue; profitability remains disputed.
